questions.q: Tampering with computer source code is an offence under —
questions.solution: **Sec 65 = source code tampering**; 43 is unauthorised access/damage; 67 is obscenity.

questions.q: Banks and research labs archive huge volumes on **magnetic tape** because it is —
options: Very cheap per TB and durable for long-term storage
questions.solution: Tape wins on **cost and longevity**, not speed — perfect for archives that are rarely read.
questions.shortcut: Archive on tape; work on disk.

questions.q: The address 127.0.0.1 refers to —
questions.solution: **127.0.0.1 = localhost** — a machine talking to itself for testing.

questions.q: In a chart, the small key that tells which colour belongs to which series is the —
questions.solution: The **legend is the chart's key** — e.g. blue = 2024, orange = 2025.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Principal congratulated the debate team ___ winning the national championship.
questions.solution: The fixed partnership is **congratulate on**: 'congratulated the team on winning'. The -ing after the blank is exactly what this frame expects.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Mischievous has **three syllables** (MIS-chi-vous) and ends **-vous**. Mischevious/mischievious insert an extra syllable — the classic error.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He asked me if I was hungry.
options: He said to me, "Are you hungry?"
He said to me, "You are hungry."
He said to me, "Was I hungry?"
He said to me, "Are I hungry?"
questions.solution: 'asked if' = yes/no question → restore quotes, question order and **present tense** (was → are), you as listener. B states instead of asking; C reverses the pronouns; D writes the impossible 'Are I'.
questions.shortcut: Reverse: if + was → Are you …? with question mark.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: 'Last month' anchors the event in finished past time, and the subject Arun is singular: **volunteered**. The other options are present, base or non-finite forms that cannot sit after a past-time adverbial in this narrative.
questions.shortcut: Time adverbial decides: 'last month' + singular subject → volunteered.
questions.passage: When Arun was small, his grandfather took him to the village post office every Saturday. The old man (1) ______ a reply to letters from his brother in Pune, and he insisted that Arun add a line of his own at the bottom. 'A letter carries your handwriting, and handwriting carries your (2) ______,' he would say. Years later, Arun, now a software engineer, still (3) ______ that yellow ink pen in his office drawer, though he rarely posts anything. Last month, when his office announced a drive to send handwritten notes to retired employees, Arun (4) ______ to write fifty of them himself. His colleagues laughed at first; later that day, half of them (5) ______ him at the desk, writing their own notes.

questions.q: **SEBI** was given statutory status by an Act of Parliament in —
questions.solution: Set up in **1988** as an executive body, SEBI became statutory under the **SEBI Act, 1992** — the Harshad Mehta scam year accelerated the change.

questions.q: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the **Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)** on 21 October 1943 at —
questions.solution: The Azad Hind Government was proclaimed in **Singapore**. The INA's HQ later moved to Rangoon; Bose had earlier worked from Berlin.

questions.q: The **'God particle'**, confirmed at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012, is the —
questions.solution: The **Higgs boson**, predicted by Peter Higgs, explains how particles acquire mass. It was hunted down at the LHC in 2012.

questions.q: **Pellagra** is caused by the deficiency of —
questions.solution: **B₃ (niacin)** — the '3 Ds': dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia (and death if untreated). Groundnut is a good source.

questions.q: The standard deviation of the data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is:
questions.solution: Mean 6; squared deviations 16, 4, 0, 4, 16; variance 8; SD $\sqrt8 = 2\sqrt2$.

questions.q: What sum of money today is equivalent to ₹1,331 payable 3 years from now, compound interest being 10% per annum?
questions.shortcut: ₹1,210 uses $1.1^2$ — three years need three chips.

questions.q: Find the LCM of $2^3 \times 3^2$ and $2 \times 3^4$.
questions.solution:
Highest powers: $2^3$ and $3^4$.
LCM $= 8 \times 81 = 648$.

questions.q: A bowler conceded runs at an average of 16 runs per wicket. In his next match he took 6 wickets for 30 runs, which lowered his average by 0.5. How many wickets had he taken before this match?
questions.shortcut: 132 is the count after the match; 63 forgets to divide by 0.5.

questions.q: In the **evening**, Ramesh's shadow falls **exactly in front of him**. Which direction is he facing?
questions.solution: Evening sun is in the West, so shadows point **East**. A shadow in front means he faces along it → **East**.
questions.shortcut: Evening shadow = East; 'in front' ⇒ facing the shadow's direction.

questions.q: Which word comes **last** in the dictionary?
questions.solution: All share PAN. 4th letters: d (Panda), e (Panel), o (Panorama), t (Pants). t is the latest → **Pants** comes last.
questions.shortcut: The biggest deciding letter wins the last slot.

questions.q: Find the value of **144 ÷ 12 ÷ 2 × 6 + 4**.
questions.solution: Left to right for ÷ and ×: 144 ÷ 12 = 12, 12 ÷ 2 = 6, 6 × 6 = 36. Then 36 + 4 = **40**. (Working 12 ÷ 2 first gives 148; working 2 × 6 first gives 5.)
questions.shortcut: Never jump to a later ÷ or ×; walk left to right.

questions.q: **In a queue of 48 people, Mohan is 30th from the front. What is his position from the back?**
questions.solution: $48 - 30 + 1$ = **19th** from the back.
questions.shortcut: Back rank = queue size − front rank + 1.
